# Vaxtly

> The local-first desktop API client. Free, open-source, MIT licensed.

Vaxtly is a desktop application for testing, debugging, and organizing HTTP requests. It runs entirely on your machine — no account, no cloud, no subscription. Team collaboration is free and unlimited, powered by Git.

## Key Features

- **REST API Client**: Full request builder with method, headers, query params, body, auth, and a syntax-highlighted editor. Import and export collections.
- **MCP Support**: Native Model Context Protocol (MCP) support. Configure MCP endpoints, discover tools, call them, inspect schemas, and see responses — the first API client with MCP built in.
- **Git Sync**: Push and pull collections to any Git remote. Share API definitions with your team through version control, not a proprietary cloud. Branch, merge, review diffs.
- **Secrets Manager**: Connect to HashiCorp Vault or AWS Secrets Manager. Secrets sync into environments at runtime — never written to disk or committed to Git.
- **Smart Environments**: Define variables per collection or folder. They auto-switch as you navigate between requests. Chain environments with inheritance and override per-folder.
- **Collections**: Organize requests into nested folders. Each collection gets its own environments, variables, and Git repository.

## Platforms

- Windows
- macOS (Homebrew: `brew install vaxtly/tap/vaxtly`)
- Linux

## Principles

- Local-first: all data stays on your machine unless you explicitly push to Git
- No account required, ever
- No telemetry or tracking
- No subscription tiers — every feature is free
- MIT licensed and open source
